title: Food and Drink: I Like, I Do Not Like
overview:
Name food and drink.
Say I like and I do not like.
Say what you want.
Ask how much a thing costs.
functions: Say what you like and do not like
Ask for food or a drink
Say you are hungry or thirsty
Ask how much a thing costs
learningPath: Patterns: I like, I do not like, I want.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 10. Today, food and drink.
First, food. Listen.
Bread. Rice. Egg. Meat. Fish. Fruit.
Say them with me. Bread. Rice. Egg.
Meat. Fish. Fruit.
Now drink. Water. Tea. Coffee. Milk.
Say them with me.
Now a new sentence. I like.
I like tea. I like fish.
Say it with me. I like.
And now the other side.
I do not like coffee.
Listen again. I do not like.
Three words. Do. Not. Like.
This is new. Until now you said no.
Now you can say a whole sentence.
Say it with me. I do not like.
Next, want. Want is not like.
I like tea, but now I want water.
Like is always. Want is now.
And in a shop or a cafe:
I want a cup of tea, please.
Or better: I would like a cup of tea.
Last, two feelings.
I am hungry. I want food.
I am thirsty. I want a drink.
And the question: How much is it?
That is Unit 10. Go and order a tea.

grammar.title: I like, I do not like
grammar.explanation:
Until now you answered no.
Now you can say a whole sentence.
I do not like takes three small words.
grammar.rule:
I like tea.
I do not like coffee.

You like fish.
You do not like meat.

He likes rice.    (he, she, it → likes)
He does not like fish.
grammar.workedExample:
You are given coffee and you do not want it.
1. Start: I.
2. Then do not.
3. Then like.
4. Then the thing: coffee.
5. Say: I do not like coffee. Thank you.
grammar.mistake:
No: I not like coffee.
English needs do.
Yes: I do not like coffee.
Short form: I don't like coffee.
grammar.practice:
Make it negative.
1. I like fish. ___
2. I like coffee. ___
3. I like meat. ___
4. I like sugar in tea. ___
grammar.answers:
1. I do not like fish.
2. I do not like coffee.
3. I do not like meat.
4. I do not like sugar in tea.
All four? You can refuse politely now.

grammar.title: Like and want are not the same
grammar.explanation:
Like is about always.
Want is about now.
Learners mix them, and it matters.
grammar.rule:
I like tea.        (always, in general)
I want tea.        (now, today)

I like coffee, but I want water now.

In a cafe you say want or would like.
Not: I like a tea.
grammar.workedExample:
You are in a cafe and you are thirsty.
1. You are asking for now, not always.
2. So use want or would like.
3. Say: I would like a cup of tea, please.
4. Not: I like a cup of tea.
5. That would mean tea in general.
grammar.mistake:
No: I like a tea, please.
Yes: I would like a tea, please.
The word a is the clue: a means one, now.
grammar.practice:
Like or want?
1. In a cafe: I ___ a coffee, please.
2. In general: I ___ coffee.
3. I am thirsty. I ___ water.
4. Fish is good. I ___ fish.
grammar.answers:
1. want (or would like)
2. like
3. want
4. like
All four? This is a mistake worth not making.

grammar.title: Ordering, and asking the price
grammar.explanation:
Two sentences carry a whole cafe.
One to ask. One to check the price.
grammar.rule:
I would like a cup of tea, please.
A glass of water, please.

How much is it?
How much are they?

It is two.
Thank you.
grammar.workedExample:
You are at a counter and you want tea.
1. Say: I would like a tea, please.
2. They make it.
3. Ask: How much is it?
4. Listen to the number.
5. Not sure? Ask: Sorry, two or twelve?
grammar.mistake:
Do not point and say nothing.
One polite sentence is enough.
And always ask the price before you pay.
grammar.tip: Please goes at the end of the ask.
grammar.practice:
Order these.
1. a tea
2. a glass of water
3. some bread
4. two eggs
grammar.answers:
Any polite form is right.
I would like a tea, please. is a good model.
Check: please in all four?
Bread takes some. Eggs take a number.

grammar.title: I am hungry. I am thirsty.
grammar.explanation:
English says you ARE hungry.
Many languages say you HAVE hunger.
That is why this one needs saying.
grammar.rule:
I am hungry.
I am thirsty.
I am tired.

Are you hungry?
Yes, I am.
No, I am not.
grammar.workedExample:
Your body wants food.
1. In English that is an adjective.
2. So use am, not have.
3. Say: I am hungry.
4. Then ask for what you need.
5. Say: I am hungry. Is there any bread?
grammar.mistake:
No: I have hungry.
No: I have hunger.
Yes: I am hungry.
grammar.tip: Hungry and thirsty take am, not have.
grammar.practice:
Write am or have.
1. I ___ hungry.
2. I ___ a cup of tea.
3. I ___ thirsty.
4. I ___ some bread.
5. I ___ tired.
grammar.answers:
1. am
2. have
3. am
4. have
5. am
Four or five right? Feelings take am. Things take have.

readings.title: What I Eat
readings.setting: A small kitchen, in the evening
readings.passage:
In the morning I eat bread.
I drink tea with milk.
I do not like coffee.
At one o'clock I am hungry.
I eat rice and fish.
In the evening I eat bread again.
I drink water.
I like fruit, so I eat fruit every day.
It is not much, but it is enough.

readings.title: A Cup of Tea, Please
readings.setting: A small cafe, in the morning
readings.passage:
Good morning. What would you like?
A cup of tea, please.
With milk?
Yes, please. And one sugar.
Anything to eat?
Some bread, please.
That is three.
Here you are.
Thank you.

readings.title: Our Prices
readings.genre: A price list on a cafe wall
readings.passage:
Tea        1
Coffee     2
Water      1
Milk       1
Bread      2
Egg        1
Fish       5

Ask at the counter.
We take cards.

comprehension.q: What does the person eat in the morning?
comprehension.why: Line 1: In the morning I eat bread.

comprehension.q: What do they drink with milk?
comprehension.why: Line 2: I drink tea with milk.
Line 3: I do not like coffee.

comprehension.q: What do they eat at one o'clock?
comprehension.why: Line 5: I eat rice and fish.

comprehension.q: Does the person eat a lot?
comprehension.why: The last line says it is enough.

comprehension.q: What does the person order to drink?
comprehension.why: Line 2: A cup of tea, please.

comprehension.q: What do they order to eat?
You want a tea and an egg. How much?
comprehension.why: Tea is 1 and an egg is 1.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Name the food
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
bread ... rice ... egg ... meat
fish ... fruit ... milk ... water
Now say them in two groups.
Food: bread, rice, egg, meat, fish, fruit.
Drink: water, tea, coffee, milk.
Tap the mic. Say both groups.
Check: ten words in all?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name three foods. Say if each is food or drink.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — I like, I do not like
speaking.instructions:
Say six lines about yourself.
Three with I like. Three with I do not like.
Use food and drink words.
Tap the mic. Say the six lines.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: did you say do not, not just not?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor two foods you like and one you do not.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Like or want?
speaking.instructions:
Tap Listen. Say like or want.
1. In a cafe, right now.
2. About food in general.
3. You are thirsty now.
4. Fish is good for you.
5. You are ordering a coffee.
6. You eat rice every day.
Tap the mic. Say six answers.
Check: want, like, want, like, want, like.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor the difference between I like tea and I want tea.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Order it
speaking.instructions:
You are in a cafe. Read A. Say B.
1. A: What would you like? B: A cup of tea, please.
2. A: With milk? B: Yes, please. And one sugar.
3. A: Anything to eat? B: Some bread, please.
4. A: That is three. B: How much is the fish?
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: please in every ask?
speaking.tutor: Order a drink and food from the tutor. Then ask the price.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — I am hungry
speaking.instructions:
Say each line out loud.
1. I am hungry.
2. I am thirsty.
3. I am not hungry.
4. Are you hungry?
5. Are you thirsty?
6. I am hungry. Is there any bread?
Tap the mic. Say the six lines.
Check: am, not have?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor you are hungry. Ask what there is to eat.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — The sound in eat and it
speaking.instructions:
Two sounds that learners mix.
Listen.
eat ... it ... eat ... it
Eat is long. It is short.
Now these pairs.
sheep ... ship
seat ... sit
Now say: I eat it.
Tap the mic. Say it three times.
Check: is the first sound longer than the last?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say eat or it. Say which one you heard.

writing.title: Writing 1 — What I eat
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about your food.
Say what you eat and drink.
Use I like and I do not like.
writing.model:
In the morning I eat bread.
I drink tea with milk.
I do not like coffee.
I like fruit.
writing.criteria:
Four lines.
Use I like once, and I do not like once.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add a line about what you eat in the evening.

writing.title: Writing 2 — A shopping list
writing.prompt:
Write a list of six things to buy.
One on each line.
Put a number or the word some before each one.
writing.model:
some bread
two eggs
some rice
one fish
some milk
some fruit
writing.criteria:
Six things.
One on each line.
A number or some before each one.
They are all food or drink.
writing.extension: Now write how much you think it will cost.

activities.title: Practice 1 — Food or drink?
activities.instructions:
Write food or drink.
1. bread
2. water
3. rice
4. tea
5. fish
6. coffee
7. egg
8. milk
activities.answers:
1. food
2. drink
3. food
4. drink
5. food
6. drink
7. food
8. drink
Six or more right: good.
activities.solo: Say your answers out loud first.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Make it negative
activities.instructions:
Change each one to I do not like.
1. I like fish.
2. I like coffee.
3. I like meat.
4. I like sugar.
5. I like milk.
6. I like eggs.
activities.answers:
1. I do not like fish.
2. I do not like coffee.
3. I do not like meat.
4. I do not like sugar.
5. I do not like milk.
6. I do not like eggs.
Five or six right: good. Do not, not just not.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Like or want?
activities.instructions:
Write like or want.
1. In a cafe: I ___ a tea, please.
2. In general: I ___ tea.
3. I am thirsty. I ___ water.
4. Fish is good. I ___ fish.
5. Right now I ___ some bread.
6. Every day I ___ rice.
activities.answers:
1. want
2. like
3. want
4. like
5. want
6. like
Five or six right: good. Want is now. Like is always.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Order it
activities.instructions:
Order each one politely.
1. a tea
2. a glass of water
3. some bread
4. two eggs
5. a coffee with milk
6. some fruit
activities.answers:
Any polite form is right.
I would like a tea, please. is a good model.
Check: please in all six?
Did you use some for bread and fruit?
activities.solo: Record all six, then listen back.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Am or have?
activities.instructions:
Write am or have.
1. I ___ hungry.
2. I ___ a cup of tea.
3. I ___ thirsty.
4. I ___ some bread.
5. I ___ tired.
6. I ___ two eggs.
activities.answers:
1. am
2. have
3. am
4. have
5. am
6. have
Five or six right: good. Feelings take am. Things take have.

activities.title: Practice 6 — How much?
activities.instructions:
Look at Our Prices in Reading 3.
1. How much is a tea?
2. How much is a coffee?
3. Which is the most expensive?
4. A tea and an egg together?
5. Can you pay with a card?
activities.answers:
1. One
2. Two
3. The fish, at five
4. Two
5. Yes
Four or five right: you can use a price list.
activities.solo: Look at the list, then answer.

quizzes.why: Tea is a drink. The others are food.

quizzes.q: It comes from a cow and it is white. It is ___.

quizzes.why: English needs do before not like.
He, she and it add s: he likes.

quizzes.q: In a cafe you say: I would ___ a tea, please.
quizzes.why: I would like is the polite way to order.
Like is general. Want is about now.

quizzes.q: You are thirsty now. You say: I ___ water.
What do you ask before you pay?
Which is the polite way to ask for bread?
quizzes.why: Please makes the ask polite, and bread takes some.

quizzes.q: Your body wants food. You say: I ___ hungry.
quizzes.why: English says you ARE hungry, not you have hunger.

quizzes.q: Your body wants a drink. You are ___.
quizzes.why: Thirsty is for drink. Hungry is for food.

quizzes.q: You drink water from it. It is a ___.
quizzes.why: A glass is for cold drinks. A cup is usually for hot ones.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: The first negative the learner builds
teacherNotes.note: Until now they have answered no. I do not like is the first time they make a negative sentence themselves, and the extra word do has no equivalent in most first languages. Expect I not like for a while and keep correcting it kindly.

teacherNotes.type: Like and want is a real problem, not a nicety
teacherNotes.note: I like a coffee, please will be understood, but I like coffee and I want a coffee mean different things and a learner who cannot separate them cannot order. Pattern 2 is the one to spend time on.

teacherNotes.type: I am hungry, not I have hunger
teacherNotes.note: A large number of languages express this with have. The correction is quick; the reason is worth giving, because it also covers thirsty, tired and cold.

teacherNotes.type: Food is personal and it is safe
teacherNotes.note: Unlike family, food is a topic every learner can speak about at length without risk, and it is the easiest place in the level to get a beginner talking. Let Speaking 2 run long if it is going well.

selfAssessment.statement: I can name food and drink.
I can say I like and I do not like.
I can say what I want.
I can order a drink and ask the price.
I can say I am hungry.
I can write about what I eat.

assignment.title: Order a drink, and say what you like
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Order a drink and something to eat.
Then say three things you like and one you do not.
2. Write four lines about what you eat in a day.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
